text: Elephants walk on their toes, with thick fibrous pads beneath their feet cushioning the load.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, Asian elephant fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/asian-elephant. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Fur on a fennec fox's paws helps with traction in sand and shields the feet from hot ground.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, fennec fox fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/fennec-fox. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: A beaver's flattened tail helps steer during swimming and brace the body on land. A slap on the water can signal danger.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, beaver fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/beaver. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Orangutans usually move through trees by careful climbing and walking, distributing their weight among branches. Their long arms and grasping feet suit this arboreal travel.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: Smithsonian National Zoo, orangutan fact sheet; https://nationalzoo.si.edu/animals/orangutan. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: Plains spadefoots spend much of the year underground. Their spadelike feet help dig the burrows used for shelter and overwintering.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone amphibians; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/amphibians.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.

text: American dippers dive into streams to take aquatic insects. A songbird's feeding ground can lie below the water's surface.
provenance: Original factual paraphrase. Source: National Park Service, Yellowstone bird inventory; https://www.nps.gov/yell/learn/nature/birds.htm. Consulted 2026-10-13.
